description: Single-panel potentiostatic polarization plot of four Fe-Mn-Al-C low-density steels in 3.5 wt% NaCl, with one enlarged inset. Main axes: x = "Time (s)", 0-8000 with ticks every 2000 s; y = "Current density (×10⁻⁴ A/cm²)", 0-8 with ticks every 2, the plot area shaded light blue to pink. Four colour-coded curves are defined in the legend at upper right: S0 (red), S950 (green), S1050 (blue) and S1150 (magenta). At t ≈ 0 all curves are at high current density - the magenta S1150 trace enters from above the top of the axis - and all fall steeply to near zero within the first few hundred seconds, then show small transient peaks between roughly 500 and 1200 s (the green S950 and magenta S1150 peaks are the largest, well below 1 ×10⁻⁴ A/cm²), after which they stay nearly flat. A red-outlined box on the curves near 6000-7200 s is linked by an arrow to an inset with x = 6400-7400 s and y = "Current density (×10⁻⁴ A/cm²)" from 0 to 0.3, which resolves the steady-state currents: S0 (red) highest, lying just below the 0.1 gridline, then S1150 (magenta), then S1050 (blue), with S950 (green) lowest. The figure demonstrates the ranking of protective oxide-film quality in the order S950 > S1050 > S1150 > S0.

observations.observation: The figure is a current density vs time curve set for four samples, with a legend at the upper right listing S0, S950, S1050 and S1150.
Legend colour coding: S0 = red, S950 = green, S1050 = blue, S1150 = magenta.
Main y-axis is labelled "Current density (×10⁻⁴ A/cm²)" and is scaled 0-8; the x-axis is labelled "Time (s)" and is scaled 0-8000.
All four curves fall steeply from a high initial current density to near the baseline within the first few hundred seconds; the magenta S1150 trace is clipped above the top of the y-axis at t ≈ 0.

Each curve shows a small transient peak in roughly the 500-1200 s interval before settling to a near-flat plateau; the green (S950) and magenta (S1150) peaks are the largest but remain below 1 ×10⁻⁴ A/cm².
The inset is a zoom of the interval 6400-7400 s on the x-axis and 0-0.3 ×10⁻⁴ A/cm² on the y-axis, connected by an arrow to a red-outlined box over the main curves at about 6000-7200 s.
Within the inset the steady-state ordering is S0 (red) highest, lying just below the 0.1 gridline, followed by S1150 (magenta), then S1050 (blue), with S950 (green) the lowest and flattest.
No numeric data labels are printed on any curve; all values must be read from the axis ticks.
The caption states the figure shows potentiostatic polarization curves of the LDSs in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution.

The citing text states that during the initial 60 s of polarization all samples exhibited a rapid current density decline to below 9 μA/cm², corresponding to surface oxide film formation and initial anodic dissolution.
The citing text states that the current density of all samples increases and then decreases during the polarization period of 600-1400 s, corresponding to rupture and self-healing of the oxide film.

The citing text gives the stable current densities as S0 = 8.39 μA/cm², S950 = 2.45 μA/cm², S1050 = 4.52 μA/cm² and S1150 = 6.04 μA/cm², with S950 achieving the lowest value and optimal corrosion protection.
The visual ordering in the inset (S0 > S1150 > S1050 > S950) is consistent with the stable current densities quoted in the citing text, although the exact numeric values are not printed on the plot.

The citing text places the rupture/self-healing oscillation at 600-1400 s, whereas the visible transient peaks on the plot appear somewhat earlier (approximately 500-1200 s); the timescale cannot be read precisely from the rendered figure.

subfigures.description: Full-range current density vs time plot (x: Time 0-8000 s; y: Current density ×10⁻⁴ A/cm², 0-8) with four curves labelled in the legend: S0 (red), S950 (green), S1050 (blue), S1150 (magenta). All curves decay from a high initial value to near zero within a few hundred seconds, show small transient peaks around 500-1200 s, then flatten near the baseline. A red-outlined rectangle marks the ~6000-7200 s interval.

Enlarged view of the highlighted 6000-7200 s interval (x: 6400-7400 s; y: Current density ×10⁻⁴ A/cm², 0-0.3) reached by an arrow. The four steady-state curves are separated: S0 (red) is highest just under 0.1, S1150 (magenta) and S1050 (blue) fall below it, and S950 (green) is the lowest and flattest.

unreadable_items: Exact numeric values of the four stable current densities are not printed on the plot or inset; they are only supplied by the citing text
Precise peak times and peak current densities of the transient 500-1200 s peaks cannot be read at the supplied resolution
